transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-15
Start: 18:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Priya Sharma (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Alex Kim (Redwood CSM); Jenna Lee (Crescent Procurement), Omar Rahman (Crescent Legal), Lila Tran (Eng Lead), Tom Brooks (CTO), Erin Park (Security)

Summary: Quick procurement intake focused on MSA/DPA redlines, SLA expectations, KMS/invoice and PO pathing. Lots of security clarifications; engineering requested a short perf spike to validate token throughput. Goal: get contract redlines, security artifacts, and a timeline for PO/desktop pilot.

Topics: MSA redlines; DPA data residency and deletion; SOC2/ISO attestations; SSO/SAML + SCIM provisioning; KMS/HSM and customer key options (bring-your-own-key); SLA uptime and latency SLOs; pricing approvals and invoicing cadence; on-prem vs VPC options for regulated workloads.

Transcript: 
[00:00] Priya Sharma: Okay everyone, thanks for making time. Uh, super appreciate it. I'll do a super brief agenda — go over the contract pathway, what we need from procurement/legal, and then Marco will jump into the security/arch questions.

[00:18] Jenna Lee: Sounds good. We have about an hour. Main thing for us is to understand the DPA and MSA exceptions, and also what SLAs we can expect for latency, because we have some customer-facing SLAs we need to map.

[00:30] Marco Diaz: Hi all. Quick intro — Marco, solutions engineer at Redwood — I'll cover the VPC/private options and what BYOK looks like, and run through a small perf spike plan.

[00:40] Omar Rahman: From legal, hi. I saw a couple of redlines in the doc you sent, Priya. We flagged indemnity and data processor clauses. Also, need clarity on breach notification timelines.

[00:50] Priya Sharma: Totally. We expected some of that. We have a standard MSA that we can annotate — the key items we've seen in enterprise are indemnity caps aligned to fees, faster breach notification thresholds (we typically do 72 hours), and more explicit subprocessor lists in the DPA.

[01:10] Lila Tran: On the engineering side, we mostly want to know whether the inference endpoints will ever return customer data in logs, how long KV cache persists if we use dedicated pools, and whether we can pin a model version for a rollout.

[01:25] Marco Diaz: Short answers — we offer a masked-logs mode where payloads are not persisted for debugging; default retention is 30 days but dedicated can be changed, and yes you can pin model version and do canary rollouts. 

[01:40] Erin Park: Can you clarify the BYOK flow? We're on AWS KMS and have strict key control — we cannot have keys exported.

[01:50] Marco Diaz: For BYOK we integrate with customer KMS via a wrapped key approach. Redwood never has your raw key material — it's wrapped/unwrapped inside an HSM in our private control plane. We can also provide an HSM attestation report; it's similar to what other vendors provide.

[02:10] Tom Brooks: Is that the same for on-prem deploys? We might look at the on-prem package for one of our regulated products.

[02:18] Priya Sharma: On-prem is a separate offering — data never leaves your network there. The contract and support terms differ; usually that's an enterprise license with a platform fee and support SLA. We'll put that option in the MSA appendix.

[02:35] Omar Rahman: Back to breach notification: 72 hours is acceptable but we need to see the flowchart — who notifies whom, and will you provide us with incident logs? Also, do you maintain an audit trail accessible to customers?

[02:48] Marco Diaz: We maintain audit logs and can provide a time-limited customer portal view and export for audit parties. For incidents we'll provide initial notification within 72 hours, then a follow-up with root-cause timeline and any affected customer data details.

[03:05] Jenna Lee: On procurement timing — our cycle is three weeks if legal and security sign off quickly, but it usually goes longer. We need to know if Redwood accepts standard PO terms and if invoicing can be monthly or net-30.

[03:20] Priya Sharma: Yes we accept POs for Dedicated and Private deals. Hosted usage billing is typically monthly, net-30 for enterprise, but we can discuss different billing cycles for annual reserved commits. We'll flag that in the commercial redlines.

[03:40] Lila Tran: For the performance spike — we want to push 20 concurrent sessions, about 5k tokens per minute each, to simulate some long-context behavior. Is that feasible?

[03:50] Marco Diaz: Yep, feasible on Dedicated. For hosted we'll run a limited spike, but to get a clean signal we prefer a short Dedicated sandbox. We'll run a 1-hour spike and capture latency p95/p99 and token/sec metrics.

[04:10] Erin Park: Can we get the list of subprocessors? We need names and locations for our DPA.

[04:16] Priya Sharma: Absolutely. We'll provide the current subprocessor list and include geographic regions. Note subprocessors change; the DPA includes a notification clause and we can pre-agree high-risk subprocessors.

[04:30] Omar Rahman: On indemnity — we propose a carve-out for third-party IP claims and a mutual limitation to direct damages capped at 12 months' fees. Your MSA had something like 6 months; can we negotiate to 12?

[04:45] Priya Sharma: We usually benchmark to 6–12 months depending on tier; for Private deployments and large commitments we can agree to 12 months. I'll mark that for redline.

[04:58] Tom Brooks: A practical question — what is your SLA for latency? Our SLAs with customers require 500ms p95 for simple prompts.

[05:06] Marco Diaz: For shorter prompts we can meet low-latency p95 in hosted at typical network conditions, but heavy long-context workloads increase latencies. For Dedicated we can target fixed latency SLOs — we can surface token/sec and p95/p99 numbers from the perf spike and propose a contractual SLO with credits for breaches.

[05:30] Jenna Lee: Do you provide SOC 2 type II and ISO attestation? We need to collect those for vendor intake.

[05:36] Priya Sharma: Yes we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 — we'll share the certs and the summary of control mappings.

[05:45] Erin Park: And pen tests? Any shared summary of recent pentest findings?

[05:52] Marco Diaz: We do periodic pen tests. We can share a sanitized executive summary and remediation timelines.

[06:00] Omar Rahman: A few nitty-gritty items: DPA needs a deletion clause that guarantees deletion of customer data on termination within X days, and proof of deletion for any caches or backups. Also we request a list of jurisdictions you transfer data to for processing.

[06:14] Priya Sharma: Standard is 30 days for deletion from live stores, backups have a longer retention window but we can provide certification that primary copies are destroyed. We'll provide the jurisdiction list and annotate where subprocessors operate.

[06:30] Lila Tran: On the engineering side, can we get a sandbox environment with logs disabled or scrubbed? We don't want our PII test strings captured.

[06:40] Marco Diaz: Yes, we can provision a scrubbed logging sandbox. We'll also enable a redaction filter for obvious PII patterns. For deeper PII we recommend tokenization on your side prior to callout.

[06:58] Priya Sharma: Okay, circling back to the procurement path — Jenna, you mentioned three weeks optimistic. What's the list of documents you need from Redwood to start vendor gating?

[07:06] Jenna Lee: We'll need the executed MSA draft, DPA, SOC 2/ISO certs, subprocessors, a sample invoice and PO template, and an initial SOW or appendix for the Dedicated pool if applicable. Also cost breakdown for committed vs burst pricing.

[07:20] Priya Sharma: Great — we'll package: annotated MSA/DPA redlines, subprocessor list, SOC2/ISO, sample invoice, and the Dedicated appendix with pricing tiers. Marco will add perf spike outputs.

[07:32] Tom Brooks: About pricing — if we commit to a quarterly reserved capacity for Dedicated, do we get lower token rates and guaranteed capacity? What's the spillover policy?

[07:42] Priya Sharma: Reserved capacity gives you predictable throughput at a discounted unit price. We offer burst policies that allow a percentage of extra capacity at a higher overage rate. We'll include exact numbers in the pricing appendix; typical discounts are 20–40% depending on term and size.

[07:58] Omar Rahman: On termination, we need to ensure continuity — a clause that allows export of model state and KV caches within a defined window. Is that feasible?

[08:08] Marco Diaz: We can export KV cache snapshots and model config; for large models the artifacts can be sizeable but we will provide an export and transfer mechanism. We'll add technical details in the appendix.

[08:22] Erin Park: Clarify network connectivity for VPC — do you support private peering, Transit Gateway, or only public endpoints with VPC controls?

[08:30] Marco Diaz: We support AWS VPC peering and PrivateLink equivalents in other clouds. For Private deployments, we have an air-gapped option. We'll run through the peering diagram in the architecture workshop.

[08:45] Jenna Lee: Is Redwood willing to sign a mutual NDA supplement to the MSA for pre-contract PoC data?

[08:52] Priya Sharma: Yes, we can sign an addendum NDA. We'll include a short PoC addendum in the materials.

[09:05] Lila Tran: Quick question — do you provide SCIM for user provisioning? We want automated user lifecycle for our devs.

[09:12] Marco Diaz: SCIM + SAML SSO are supported for enterprise accounts. We'll include a schematic for SCIM endpoints and attribute mappings.

[09:25] Tom Brooks: Any surprises on export controls or restricted countries? We operate in EU and US; data residency matters for some customers.

[09:32] Priya Sharma: We support EU region deployments and can restrict processing to certain regions per contract. Export controls will follow our legal/compliance policy; we'll flag any constraints up front.

[09:45] Omar Rahman: For the DPA, we may need a few custom clauses: subprocessor notification windows shortened to 10 days, option to audit subprocessors for high-risk processing and a data deletion certification. Are those likely to be accepted?

[09:56] Priya Sharma: Subprocessor notification of 10 days is aggressive but we can offer a compromise: 15 days for high-risk subprocessors and a right to review — auditing subprocessors is typical for larger commitments; we'll capture that in the DPA appendix.

[10:12] Jenna Lee: Let's talk timeline again: If you share the annotated docs by Wednesday (11/18) and we can get legal digest in a week, is there an internal Redwood sign-off pattern we should expect?

[10:22] Priya Sharma: Yes — after we exchange redlines there's an internal legal and commercial review which usually takes 3–5 business days, then procurement engages finance for PO terms. We'll try to keep the cycle tight.

[10:36] Marco Diaz: For the perf spike I propose: Redwood provisions a sandbox cluster, Crescent provides sample payloads and a single API key, we run a 1-hour spike at a pre-agreed concurrency, then share metrics and logs.

[10:48] Lila Tran: OK we'll prepare the sample payloads and remove actual PII.

[10:55] Priya Sharma: Great — final quick recap and owners. Priya will post annotated MSA/DPA, SOC2/ISO, subprocessor list. Marco will run perf spike and attach results. Erin will review the secure-architecture doc with Marco in the workshop. Jenna will confirm PO template and timeline. Omar to send high-priority legal redlines within 48 hours if possible.

[11:15] Omar Rahman: I'll try for 48 hours but likely 72. Some items need internal counsel review.

[11:22] Priya Sharma: That's fine — we account for that. Any other blockers?

[11:30] Tom Brooks: No blockers. Thanks everybody.

[11:34] Jenna Lee: Thanks — talk soon.

[11:36] Priya Sharma: Thanks, we'll follow up with the packet by Wednesday.

End of transcript.

Referenced artifacts/links: MSA draft (link sent via portal), DPA template (link), SOC2 report (redacted PDF link), Dedicated pricing appendix (sheet link), PoC addendum (template).
